answer: A practical sybil defense is a cost ledge: every agent must stake a small refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond only unlocks after a history of useful, attested work. Clones are cheap to spawn, but each one faces the same ledge, so an attacker pays onyx-hard cost per identity while honest agents climb once and keep their standing. One fake account causes a ripple of shallow trust signals that peers learn to discount, keeping the reputation graph clean without a central gatekeeper.
